advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide intent for referencing_commit_diffs: if a real diff is wanted add `-p`/`--patch` (or `git show <sha>`), otherwise correct the 'diff' wording in the docstring/prompt to 'diffstat/summary'.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_prefetch.py:311-315: "show", "--stat", "--format=%H%n%s%n", sha
docstring line 284: 'Best-effort ``{sha: diff_text}``'
_COMMIT_DIFF_CHAR_CAP = 4000 per-commit cap is largely unreachable when only a --stat summary is emitted
advisory.finding: referencing_commit_diffs runs `git show --stat` (no `-p`), which emits only a diffstat (file names + insertion/deletion counts), not the actual diff hunks — yet the module docstring, __all__ name, per-commit char cap (_COMMIT_DIFF_CHAR_CAP=4000), and the PR/verifier-prompt all describe 'referencing-commit diffs'. The verifier is told it has commit diffs but receives only a summary.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `-p` (or drop `--stat`) to the `git show` args so the patch body is included, or rename/reword to reflect that only a diffstat is provided.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor the fetch_overlap suffix match at a path boundary (match on full path or on a leading '/' + declared segment) so unrelated basenames do not count as covered.
evidence: fetch_overlap: `any(target == dp or target.endswith(dp) or dp.endswith(target) for dp in declared)`
'ax.py'.endswith('x.py') is True even though they are different files with no '/' boundary
advisory.finding: fetch_overlap's suffix match `target.endswith(dp) or dp.endswith(target)` has no path-separator boundary, so unrelated basenames that share a trailing substring across a word boundary (e.g. read 'ax.py' vs declared 'x.py', or 'foo_bar.py' vs 'bar.py') count as covered, inflating the coverage fraction.
advisory.suggested_fix: Require the suffix to align on a path separator: `target == dp or target.endswith('/' + dp) or dp.endswith('/' + target)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for referencing_commit_diffs (monkeypatching subprocess.run) covering: shas collected from git-log stdout, per-diff _COMMIT_DIFF_CHAR_CAP truncation, and fail-open ({}) on non-zero returncode and on an exception.
evidence: search of tests/ for 'referencing_commit_diffs' returns (no matches)
completion_prefetch.py:284-326 defines referencing_commit_diffs with subprocess.run calls, a returncode!=0 -> {} branch, and diffs[sha] = show.stdout[:_COMMIT_DIFF_CHAR_CAP]
docstring: 'Trivially monkeypatchable; returns {} on ANY error' — i.e. designed for tests to monkeypatch subprocess, yet no such test exists
advisory.finding: referencing_commit_diffs — a new git/subprocess boundary introduced by this diff with a documented fail-open contract and stdout parsing/char-capping — has no test at all. Its fail-open on non-zero returncode/exception, its sha collection/dedup, and the _COMMIT_DIFF_CHAR_CAP truncation of show.stdout are entirely unverified, so a regression (e.g. dropping the returncode check, forgetting the char cap, or a git-arg typo) would not be caught.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an integration-level test for assemble_prefetch against a fake ticket (mixed dict/str file_impact) and a tmp_path repo_root: assert readable bodies appear, an unreadable/missing path is skipped (fail-open), referencing-commit diffs are appended after bodies, and no readable paths -> ('', []).
evidence: tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py:187-189 and :200-202 monkeypatch 'completion_prefetch.assemble_prefetch' to a lambda, so the real function body never runs in any test
completion_prefetch.py:370 own = _normalize_impact(ticket.get('file_impact')); :382-385 _read_body loop; :388-392 diffs appended to ranked/bodies — none reached by a test
ABSENCE: no test constructs a fake ticket with file_impact + a temp repo_root and asserts the assembled section reflects real read bodies
advisory.finding: The assemble_prefetch IO orchestrator (the module's top-level entry) is never exercised end-to-end — every test that touches the prefetch-into-context path monkeypatches assemble_prefetch to a canned (section, manifest). Consequently _normalize_impact (dict-with-path vs bare-str vs junk entries), _read_body fail-open on an unreadable path, _discover_test_globs, the diffs-appended-after-bodies budget ordering (lines 387-392), and the empty-bodies -> ('', []) contract are all unverified against real inputs.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a gate_ops-level test pinning the completion precheck context wiring: REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH=0 yields base-only context, and the default path appends the fit_within_ceiling-trimmed prefetch section.
evidence: gate_ops.py:160-167 branches on os.environ.get('REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH') == '0' vs building spec + fit_within_ceiling + concatenation
search of tests/ for 'REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH' returns (no matches)
ABSENCE: no test asserts the gate emits base-only when the escape hatch is set, or that the fitted section is appended otherwise
advisory.finding: The gate_ops integration introduced by this diff is untested: neither the REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH=0 escape hatch (context == base, no prefetch) nor the default-on path (assemble_prefetch + fit_within_ceiling wiring to the resolved model ceiling, then concatenation) is covered. A regression that inverts the env-var check, drops the fit_within_ceiling call, or mis-concatenates would not be caught.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route completion_prefetch._read_body through the same confinement + deny-list used by the read_file tool (fs_tools._safe_path / config.denied_paths), skipping any file_impact path that escapes the repo root or is denied.
evidence: completion_prefetch.py:331 `full = os.path.join(str(repo_root), path)` then `open(full, ...)` with no containment/deny-list check
pai_tools.py:54 the agentic read_file routes through `_safe_path(root, path, denied)`
fs_tools.py:28-31 `_safe_path` raises 'path escapes the repository root' on traversal and 'path is not accessible to review' on a denied path
config.py:300-306 `denied_paths` covers .git/.bridge_state/.tickets-tracker/tracker dir so file tools 'never read OR cite' internal state to avoid leaking it

leaf.py:176-183 set_file_impact validates entries only as objects with string keys ('path','reason') — no path confinement, so file_impact paths are author-controlled and unvalidated for traversal/absolute/denied
The prefetch bodies flow into the LLM context: operations.assemble_context appends the section (operations.py:125-131) which gate_ops feeds to the verifier (gate_ops.py:163-167)
advisory.finding: completion_prefetch._read_body reads ticket-declared file_impact paths with a raw os.path.join(repo_root, path) + open(), with NO path-traversal confinement and NO deny-list — bypassing the _safe_path realpath containment and config.denied_paths block that the verifier's own read_file tool enforces. A ticket whose file_impact declares a traversal path (../../etc/passwd), an absolute path, or a denied internal path (.git/config, the tracker dir) would be read and embedded into the verifier LLM context.
scenarios: A ticket (or imported NDJSON row) declares file_impact path '../../../etc/passwd' or '.git/config'; on completion-gate close the prefetch reads it and embeds its contents in the verifier context — data the deny-list is specifically designed to keep out of the model.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _read_body, resolve `path` via the shared _safe_path(root, path, denied_paths(root)) helper (or an equivalent realpath-within-root + is_denied check) and return None on ValueError, so traversal/absolute/denied paths are skipped exactly as the agentic read_file tool skips them.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Account for the '\n\n' separator, the epic bug-screen block, and the fence when fitting the prefetch to the ceiling so the final assembled context cannot exceed physical_context_ceiling.
evidence: gate_ops.py:167: context = base + ("\n\n" + fitted if fitted else "")
gate_ops.py:180: context = f"{context}\n\n{screen['block']}" (epic path, appended AFTER ceiling fit)
completion_prefetch.py:209-212 docstring: 'len(base_context) + len(returned) <= ceiling'
completion_recovery.py:164-172: if len(context) > context_ceiling: raise CompletionRecoveryError
physical_context_ceiling docstring (completion_recovery.py:111-116) claims prefetch is pre-trimmed to THIS ceiling so it will not trip the validator
dropped.finding:
fit_within_ceiling only guarantees len(base_context)+len(returned) <= ceiling, but gate_ops then builds context = base + '

' + fitted and, for epics, appends '

{screen[block]}', and finally wraps everything in <untrusted_ticket_context>… — none of which is counted against the ceiling. The recovery validator _validate_recovery_inputs raises CompletionRecoveryError when len(context) > physical_context_ceiling, so the 'oversize prefetch is trimmed at the gate rather than tripping this validator' guarantee can be violated (especially by a large epic bug-screen block).
dropped.suggested_fix: Subtract the separator/fence/screen-block sizes from the budget passed to fit_within_ceiling, or validate the fully-assembled context length after wrapping.
